clue.text: Ineffectual fellow in temporary store

definitions.meaning: in computing, a memory area holding data briefly while it is moved

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a dim old codger, and a holding area for data in transit.

clue.text: Resent move to restrict English and Greek

indicators.note: to restrict means the word for move holds the other letters inside

parts.note: budge means move, as in won't budge

explanation.surface: Someone resents a measure to limit the English and Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to resent someone having something, a close synonym.

clue.text: Criminal making foul noise

indicators.note: making means the letters are used to make something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A crook gives himself away by making a horrible sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are needed; 'making' rearranges FOUL NOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious means relating to felony, so criminal in nature.

clue.text: Produce engravings and other things — with a bit of help

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and other things

indicators.note: a bit of means only the first letter of help is used

explanation.surface: An engraver makes prints, along with other things, with a little help.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to make engravings by biting lines into metal with acid.

clue.text: Choose odd alloy

parts.note: to choose is to elect
rum is a dated British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pick out a strange metal mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrum is a natural alloy of gold and silver, used for early coins.

clue.text: A rhetorical device TS Eliot deployed

indicators.note: deployed means the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A figure of speech that the poet T S Eliot used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges TS ELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, as in not bad for good.

clue.text: Winged creatures all over France? Canards!

indicators.note: all over means scattered everywhere, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: canards are false reports, lies

explanation.surface: Flying creatures said to be everywhere in France are dismissed as hoaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' rearranges FRANCE as CRANEF. 'Canards' tempts as French ducks, but means false rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: Crane flies, or daddy-long-legs, are long-legged winged insects.

clue.text: Jane's half-cut with port wine

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous port

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of Jane is kept

explanation.surface: Jane gets a bit drunk on port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, apt with port, but means half the word. Note the pieces join as RIO then JA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Country formerly in the Himalayas

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the letters of the Himalayas

explanation.surface: A nation that once lay in the mountain range of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the Himalayas' reads as geography, but the letters are inside HiMALAYAs.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaya was the former name of the country now forming part of Malaysia.

clue.text: He has a young boxer, perhaps, to collect

parts.note: a pup is a young dog, of which a boxer is one breed

explanation.surface: A man owns a boxer puppy and goes to pick it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed, so a young one is a pup.
explanation.definitionFit: To heap up is to pile together, so to collect or amass.

clue.text: A little bird — or a hundred others

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: One small bird is compared with a hundred more of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but is the heraldic term for gold, which gives the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is Britain's smallest bird, a tiny songbird with a yellow head stripe.

clue.text: Bikini, for example, completely covering both ends of torso

indicators.note: covering means the word for completely goes round the other piece

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

indicators.note: both ends of torso means its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A swimsuit that fully covers the top and bottom of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' suggests swimwear to suit 'torso', but it is the Pacific island ring used for nuclear tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll is a Pacific coral ring, so Bikini is an example of one.

clue.text: British sailors going aboard American vessels

indicators.note: going aboard means the sailors get inside the American abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: Royal Navy sailors board ships of the US fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships to suit the sailors, but here it means containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, vessels in the sense of pots.

clue.text: Supplier of drugs once or a chap yet distributing?

indicators.note: distributing means the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a fellow is still handing things out, perhaps as a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributing' rearranges the letters of OR A CHAP YET.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was the old name for a pharmacist who made up and sold medicines.

clue.text: Monster or a mad scientist

indicators.note: mad means the letters are deranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Either a monster or a crazy scientist, as in a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad scientist' is a stock phrase, but 'mad' rearranges MONSTER OR A.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer is a scientist who studies stars and planets.

clue.text: Paintwork somewhere in Derbyshire?

parts.note: gloss is a shiny kind of paint
op, short for opus, is a work, as in a musical piece

explanation.surface: A question about decorating, asking whether the paintwork is from a Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Paintwork' has to be read as two, paint plus work. Derbyshire is an English county in the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossop is a town in the High Peak area of Derbyshire, so it is somewhere there.

clue.text: Some legal issue about farm production

indicators.note: about means the run is read backwards
some of means only a run of the letters in these words is used

explanation.surface: Part of a legal dispute concerns something produced on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'legal issue' is EGALIS; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fodder made on the farm by fermenting green crops, a product of farming.

clue.text: One of the family beginning to grumble about a dig

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of grumble is used

parts.note: re means about, as in re your letter
a dig is a jibe, a taunt

explanation.surface: A relative starts to grumble over a jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, a member of the wider family.

clue.text: I speak ill of Manxman, for example

parts.note: to slander is to speak ill of someone

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to bad-mouthing a man from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manxman comes from the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on the Isle of Man, so he is an example of an island-dweller.

clue.text: Ringleader captured in a feigned retreat

indicators.note: captured in means the leader's letter is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: sham means feigned or pretended
the leader, or first letter, of Ring is R

explanation.surface: A gang's ringleader was caught when the gang only pretended to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks military to suit 'captured' and 'feigned', but it means a place of seclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a religious retreat or hermitage in India.

clue.text: Lawman sounding warlike

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said aloud like another

parts.note: martial means warlike

explanation.surface: A sheriff whose voice sounds combative.
explanation.definitionFit: A US marshal is a federal law officer, a lawman of Western films.

clue.text: Police find Lord Emsworth initially in Lords

indicators.note: in means the initials go inside the word for Lords

parts.note: peers are members of the House of Lords

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of Lord Emsworth are taken

explanation.surface: Police track down a fictional earl in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Emsworth is P G Wodehouse's absent-minded earl of Blandings Castle; 'Lords' means members of the House of Lords, not cricket's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelers is old British slang for policemen, after Robert Peel who founded the Met.

clue.text: Hair ointment produced by the Post Office?

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: A hair cream that is made by the postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment for styling the hair.

clue.text: Each pastrycook's product with excellent crust?

indicators.note: crust means the word for excellent forms an outer shell round the other piece

parts.note: ace means excellent
a pie is what a pastrycook makes

explanation.surface: Each pie a pastry cook bakes has a superb crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means each, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: Mum or dad, for example, plead with minor going astray

indicators.note: going astray means the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Parents beg alongside a child who is wandering off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astray' rearranges the letters of PLEAD and MINOR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum and dad read the same backwards and forwards, so each is an example of such a word.

clue.text: Composer providing catalogue for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is as heard

parts.note: a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A composer draws up a catalogue for the accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' suggests accountants but means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Retreating before volcano

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: People retreat before an erupting volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, the best known in crosswords.

clue.text: Skilful Lancashire opener in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means the opener goes inside the name

parts.note: Abe is the first name of Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A skilled Lancashire opening batsman playing in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests a cricket opening batsman; Lancashire is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilful or competent.

clue.text: Poems about a racecourse

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Verses written on the subject of a horse-racing track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'on the subject of' but signals a rearrangement of POEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is the racecourse that holds the Derby.

clue.text: Resistant to change, I'd be turned into a dog

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the dog

parts.note: a hound is a dog

indicators.note: turned means the letters are switched round

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn worries that they would be transformed into a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistant to change' sits at the start; the rest reads as a person fearing transformation, but 'turned' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound describes someone narrow and conventional, stuck in fixed ways.

clue.text: All rent I collected goes to cathedral

indicators.note: collected means the letters are gathered up in a fresh order

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a cathedral city

explanation.surface: A landlord's collected rent is handed over to the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' rearranges RENT I to ENTIR; 'goes to' joins on ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly, so it can stand for all in a phrase like all alone.

clue.text: Superior gambler

definitions.meaning: one who bets, someone placing wagers

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both of higher quality and a person who places wagers.
